title: docs: a lookup option’s `description` is declared by the spec; filter-ui lists `multi-select` (objectui#10769, objectui#10779)

## objectui#10769: `content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx`, the static-option paragraph

The paragraph still described the `@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0 boundary: `SelectOptionSchema` strict over five keys, `description` refused by name, authoring it failing the whole field. Measured in this worktree's own install (`@objectstack/spec` resolved from `packages/types`, `./data` export, the version the lockfile pins), one `safeParse` each way:

| payload | verdict |
|---|---|
| `SelectOptionSchema` key set | `color, default, description, label, value, visibleWhen` |
| option `label` + `value` (control) | accepted |
| option + `description` | accepted |
| option + `icon` | refused, `unrecognized_keys` naming `icon` |
| select `FieldSchema` whose option carries `description` | accepted |
| select `FieldSchema` whose option carries `icon` | refused, `unrecognized_keys` at path `options`, `0` |

What the paragraph says now, and why each part is worded the way it is:

- **Declared on both faces.** `SelectOptionMetadata` in `@object-ui/types`, and `@objectstack/spec` as `SelectOptionSchema.description`, citing the option-A ruling on objectui#6140 / objectui#6153 (both answer 200 on a REST single-card read). An option carrying it is accepted in an authored object document.
- **What the widget does with it.** Re-read `LookupField.tsx`: the `filteredOptions` memo matches a static option on `opt.description` alongside `opt.label` (the no-data-source path, which is the static-option path the paragraph sits under). The popover row renders `option.label` plus preview columns and does not print a static option's `description`, so the page claims the search and nothing more. The sentence carrying that ("secondary text the picker's typeahead searches alongside the label") was already accurate and is unchanged.
- **The option is still strict.** An undeclared key such as `icon` is refused by name and, because `FieldSchema` routes `options` through the option schema, fails the whole field. The parenthesis notes that `SelectOptionMetadata` does carry `icon`, objectui-side only, because the page's own Field Schema section tells readers static options are `SelectOptionMetadata`, and an annotated literal with `icon` compiles.
- **No key list.** The old paragraph rotted precisely because it copied the key set into prose. Per AGENTS.md commandment #9 the page now points at the instrument: `select-option-spec-extension-7014.test.ts` re-derives both verdicts against the installed spec. This departs from the dispatch's optional suggested route (list the six keys); declared as a deviation in the report.
- **No 422.** The HTTP status was not measured here, so the page says the whole field fails, which the `FieldSchema` reading above shows.
- **The spec claim is now gate-checked.** Spelling `SelectOptionSchema.description` in a sentence that names `@objectstack/spec` puts it under the prose rule of `check:spec-symbols`, which resolves it against the installed spec. Ablation, run after the commit: `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (objectstack) replaced that citation with `SelectOptionSchema.icon` (anchor x1 to x0, blob `5be26e387283` to `4022b7e048cb`), and `check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` went red naming it ("1 passage cites a spec member the spec does not declare: `SelectOptionSchema.icon` content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx"); restore leg: blob back to the HEAD blob `5be26e387283`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## objectui#10779: `content/docs/components/complex/filter-ui.mdx`, the Schema block

`filters[].type` in the Schema block gains `'multi-select'`, in the TS face's order. Compared mechanically (quoted members extracted from each line): doc block, `FilterUISchema.filters[].type` in `packages/types/src/views.ts`, and the zod mirror in `packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts` all read `text | number | select | multi-select | date | date-range | boolean`, ordered-equal. `FilterUI` has a `case 'multi-select'` control. The "Retired: `filters[].operator`" paragraph is untouched.

## Acceptance notes

Observations, not filed:

1. `check:doc-types` is green, but it does not read the members of this union: its literal count is 1142 before and after the edit. It judges component `type` literals, and a filter-control vocabulary is not one, so for objectui#10779 the member-for-member comparison above is the reading and the gate's green is not. Carrier: none.
2. A comment in `scripts/__tests__/check-spec-symbol-derivation.test.ts` calls its repaired-wording fixture "the wording `content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx` carries today". After this PR the page no longer carries that wording. The fixture is inline and the test stays green; only the comment is now out of date. Outside this dispatch's file surface. Carrier: none.
3. `filter-ui.mdx`'s opening sentence ("text, select, date, and boolean inputs") under-lists the controls. Outside objectui#10779's scope, which is the Schema block's union. Carrier: none.
4. The `date-range` exemption for `filter-ui.mdx` in `scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs` justifies itself with cross-file line addresses that now point at unrelated lines. That is the objectui#8875 class, which is repaired opportunistically and not swept. Carrier: none.

Handed to the seat in the report (not touched here, outside `content/docs/**`): the pending changeset `.changeset/6140-field-metadata-rows-option-description.md` still says the spec refuses option `description` and `rows` by name. The installed spec accepts both, measured here, so that text would ship to the changelog false.
